_exec_summary.SummaryText:
1. Executive Summary
ONEOK Bearkat Processing Plant is in Glasscock County, Texas. Its coordinates are 31.957014°N,
-101.490136°W. The address for the facility is 4696 Ranch Road 33, Garden City, TX 79739.
Bearkat Gas Processing Plant consists of inlet separation and filtration, amine gas treating and
regeneration, glycol gas treating and regeneration, molecular sieve dehydration and regeneration,
cryogenic processing units, refrigeration compressors, condensate stabilization, residue
compression, hot oil systems, and all associated utilities and ancillary systems. Treated natural gas
from residue compression are sent offsite via pipeline. Condensate recovered from extraction process
is stored in Condensate Storage Tanks.
Bearkat Plant (or Facility) is subject to 40 CFR Part 68 because it consists of more than the threshold
quantity of a regulated flammable substance (10,000 pounds). The total regulated flammable
substance at the facility is 2,679,421 lbs. (including piping, 10% equipment inventory) plus 3251 lbs.
of methanol. The Facility does not store any toxic substances above threshold quantities. The table
below lists the regulated substances.

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Risk Management Plan (RMP) rule defines three
program levels based on processes relative potential for public impacts and the level of efforts needed
to prevent accidents. For each Program level, the rule defines requirements that reflect the level of
risk and effort associated with the processes at that level. The Program levels are as follows (from
RMP Chapter 2):
Program 1: Processes which would not affect the public in the case of a worst-case release
(in the language of Part 68, processes with no public receptors within the distance to an
endpoint from a worst-case release) and with no accidents wit

h specific offsite consequences
within the past five years are eligible for Program 1, which imposes limited hazard assessment
requirements and minimal prevention and emergency response requirements.
Program 2: Processes not eligible for Program 1 or subject to Program 3 are placed in  Program 2, which imposes streamlined prevention program requirements, as well as
additional hazard assessment, management, and emergency response requirements.
Program 3: Processes not eligible for Program 1 and either subject to OSHA's PSM standard
under federal or state OSHA programs or classified in one of ten specified North American
Industrial Classification System (NAICS) codes are placed in Program 3, which imposes
OSHAs PSM standard as the prevention program as well as additional hazard assessment,
management, and emergency response requirements.
Bearkat Plant was determined to be Program Level 3. The facility is not eligible for Program level
1 as the public receptors are located within the distance to endpoint of 1 psi overpressure from a
vapor cloud explosion in worst case release scenario. In addition, Bearkat facility is not eligible for
Program level 2 because the facility is subject to OSHA PSM standard.
2. Off-Site Consequences Analysis (40 CFR PART 68.165)
Per EPA RMP Rule 40 CFR 68, the offsite consequence analysis consists of two scenarios:
? Worst Case Release Scenario analysis to determine the greatest distance to an endpoint
resulting from an accidental release of regulated flammable or toxic substances from covered
processes.
? Alternative Release Scenario analyzes at least one alternative release scenario for each
regulated toxic substance held in a covered process(es) and at least one alternative release
scenario to represent all flammable substances held in covered processes.
For Program level 3, a worst-case release scenario and an alternative release scenario are analyzed.
Bearkat facility has no RMP-regulated toxic substances stored above RMP threshold qu

antities;
therefore, the offsite consequences analysis only considered flammable substances.
2.1. Worst-Case Release Scenario
This Facility is required to complete one worst- case release scenario per 40 CFR 68.165(a) (1). The
worst-case release scenario is determined in accordance with the requirements provided in 40 CFR
68.22(a), (b) and 40 CFR 68.25(b), (f).
As described in 40 CFR Part 68.25(b), the worst-case release shall be the greater of the following: (1)
the greatest amount held in a single vessel or (2) the greatest amount in a pipe. It is assumed that the
quantity of flammable substance is released resulting in vapor cloud explosion.
Worst-Case Release Scenario:
Condensate Storage Tank T-130A or T-130B or T-130C or T-130D (OSBL PID 011325-M2030):
Tank Dimensions: 15.5 ft. Diameter x 30 ft. Height, 1000 Barrels (42000 Gallons)
Estimated flammable Mixture (based on 100% liquid level): 232541 lbs.  

2.2 Alternative Release Scenario
This Facility required to complete one alternative release scenario per 40 CFR Part 68.165(a) (2). The
alternative release scenario considered in accordance with the guidelines provided in 40 CFR 68.22
and 40 CFR 68.28.
The alternate case release scenarios is based on 6 flange on Demethanizer Product Surge Tank V-404 (PID CRYO SC6-235) fails resulting in 0.25-inch gap. Estimated release rate of 4787 lb./min for 10 minutes of flammable mixture. The release parameters for the worst-case release are presented in Table 3. for Vapor Cloud Explosions
3. Prevention Program
Bearkat facility has implemented the prevention requirements subject to Program level 3. The
Facilitys Prevention Program 3 elements, as required under 40 CFR 68 Subpart D, are included in
the Facilitys PSM Plan, which is kept on-site as a separate document. Required elements include:
 Employee Participation (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.83

; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (c))
 Process Safety Information (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.65; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (d))
 Process Hazard Analysis (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.67; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (e))
 Operating Procedures (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.69; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (f))
 Training (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.71; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (g))
 Contractors (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.87; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (h))
 Pre-startup Review (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.77; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (i))
 Mechanical Integrity (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.73; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (j))
 Hot Work Permits (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.85; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (k))
 Management of Change (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.75; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (l))
 Incident Investigation (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.81; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (m))
 Emergency Response (EPA RMP, Subpart E; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (n))
 Compliance Audits (EPA RMP, 40 CFR, 68.79; OSHA PSM, 29 CFR 1910.119 (o))
Refer to ONEOK PSM manual for details covering PSM elements.
4. Five-Year Accident History
Bearkat Facility has had no accidental releases of flammable materials regulated under the RMP
program that resulted in deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on-site, or off-site deaths,
injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage or any environmental impact for the period
of five (5) years.
5. Emergency Response Program
The Emergency Response Program requirements for Program 3 Facilities are very similar to those
required under the PSM rule. The Emergency Response Program required under the RMP and PSM
rules must be site-specific and comprehensive, including the following elements:
 Public and emergency response agency notification procedures.
 Proper first aid and emergency medical treatment.
 Emergency response measures.
 Procedures for inspecting, testing, and maintaining emergency response equipment.
 Employee training; and
 Program review procedures.
Bearkat Facility maintains an Emergency Response Pl

an (ERP) as described in 40 CFR 68.95 that
provides guidance for emergencies expected at the Facility. In addition, operating procedures and
equipment design codes and standards associated with the operations at the Facility are
maintained.  
Furthermore, the Facility response program includes:
? Local emergency response notifications with Glasscock County LEPC and Garden City
Volunteer Fire Department
? First-aid treatment through trained personnel
? Emergency response procedures
? Coordination with community through Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC)
? Prompt response to requests for additional information from local officials.
A site map, SDSs, and a list of chemicals kept on-site are maintained at the Facility. Complete details
on the Emergency Response Program required under the PSM rule are included in Bearkat Facilitys
PSM Plan, which is kept on-site as a separate document. Bearkat Facility operating personnel are
trained to isolate the point of release and coordinate response activities with third-party responders.
6. Safety Improvements
ONEOK has a continued commitment to updating equipment and improving safety pertaining to the covered process when necessary.
